To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the diversity of grassland ecosystems is strongly threatened by land abandonment, eutrophication and climate change and (ii) the effects of these drivers are highly context-dependent and can even be countervailing.

(i) grassland biodiversity is strongly affected by the interplay between abiotic and biotically induced environmental changes; (ii) the effects are highly variable across spatial and temporal gradients; (iii) the effects are mediated by species interactions, and (iv) species-specific responses are often driven by intraspecific plastic responses to the changing environments.

(1) species diversity is strongly affected by abiotic and biotically driven processes; (2) the effects of eutrophication, abandonment, and climate change are complex and not always predictable; (3) the effects of these factors are not necessarily additive; (4) the effects of climate change on grassland biodiversity are not homogenous over Europe and differ strongly between species and communities; and (5) intraspecific plastic responses are important to buffer effects of climate change.
